entities.summary:
Mariangelo Accursio (or Accorso), born in L'Aquila, Italy, and dying there on August 4, 1546, emerged as a preeminent Italian humanist, philologist, and textual critic during the High Renaissance. His rigorous scholarship, particularly in the recovery and emendation of classical Latin texts, profoundly influenced the development of modern textual criticism. Operating at the intellectual epicenter of 16th-century Italy, Accursio's work provided foundational improvements to the understanding of ancient authors, thereby shaping the trajectory of classical studies for generations of scholars and contributing significantly to the broader Renaissance project of rediscovering antiquity.

Accursio's most celebrated achievement was his 1533 critical edition of Ammianus Marcellinus's *Res Gestae*, a monumental undertaking based on his discovery and meticulous study of the unique *Codex Hersfeldensis*. This manuscript, believed to be the sole surviving source for a significant portion of Ammianus's history, allowed Accursio to produce a text vastly superior to previous corrupt editions. Beyond Ammianus, his *Diatribae in Ausonium, Solinum, et Ovidium* (1524) showcased his exceptional philological acumen, offering incisive corrections and annotations to the works of these prominent Roman poets and geographers. He also authored *Osci et Volsci* (1524), an early work of comparative linguistics exploring ancient Italic languages, demonstrating a breadth of scholarly interest.
